method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across trust joined with work, means and consultation; trustworthiness and service; courage with protection and discretion; grief and consolation; detachment from possessions and approval; recognition and moral response; prayers of dependence; steadfastness under imprisonment and opposition; remembrance and gratitude in daily life; and companionship and humility before an open future. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: Know then that other than the kind Lord there is no faithful friend. God willing, He will show solicitude and grant boundless joy to the grieving heart. Place your trust in Him and be free from all else. Reliance on ministers is a burden and trust in princes is the greatest abasement. O friend, know this: no one but God can help man.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches that apart from God there is no faithful friend, and that reliance on ministers is a burden and trust in princes abasement; a pointed critique of misplaced trust.

selected.text: In all matters place thy trust in God and detach thyself from all else but Him. In these grievous days when the intoxication of existence hath encompassed all creation, be not heedless of the celestial realm of His love's constancy, and like unto the sun, shine forth with the effulgences of the love of the Sovereign Lord of names and attributes
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids trust and detachment in grievous days when the intoxication of existence has encompassed creation, and bids shining like the sun; steadfastness in hard times.

selected.text: And regarding thy intention to engage in the occupation thou mentioned - although from the divine perspective, any occupation thou engage in is beloved, yet if thou findest a better one, it would be higher and more beloved in the sight of God. Place thy trust in all matters upon Him and commit them to Him. Verily He is with His trusting servants.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh answers an inquiry about an occupation, saying any occupation is beloved yet a better one more so, and bids trust and committal of all matters; personal vocational counsel the arc cites.

selected.text: The Most Exalted Pen hath, throughout the nights and days, made mention of those who have turned towards Him and summoned them to the divine path. Some among the people remained heedless, some turned away, and a few set their faces toward the highest horizon and quaffed from the living waters which are the recognition of God, exalted be His glory.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describes how some remained heedless, some turned away and a few set their faces toward God and drank of His recognition; the range of response the arc traces.

selected.text: Now, thou shouldst, also, never be grieved. Rely upon God. Trust Him. Rest assured in His Bounty and Mercy, and know surely that when serving God, the doors of relief wilt thou see open before thee, and all the people of the earth shall be unable to prevent thee, because when man is serving the Kingdom, he is under the protection and shelter of God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids the recipient never grieve but rely on God, assured that one serving the Kingdom finds doors of relief and is under God’s protection; ties trust to service.

selected.text: Grieve not over the world and its hardships, but place thy trust in all matters in thy Lord. Verily, He preserveth whosoever trusteth in Him and seeketh His aid. He will assist thee with the means of the heavens and earth, and will send down from the clouds of grace that which will draw thee nigh unto Him and distance thee from all who deny and deviate.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids not grieving over the world’s hardships, since God preserves those who trust Him and assists with the means of heaven and earth; means and trust together.

selected.text: The Wronged One maketh mention of thee and commandeth thee that which shall profit thee throughout the kingdom of earth and heaven, namely to commit thy affairs unto Him and place thy trust in Him. Verily He is the Almighty, the Unconstrained. He is with those who love Him and remembereth those who remember Him and aideth those who turn unto Him. He is the All
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a recipient that what will profit him is to commit his affairs to God, Who remembers those who remember Him; an individual encounter with assurance.

selected.text: Resignation to the Will of God is the soul of happiness and the link connecting the most opposite characters. When a soul acquires the quality of resignation the outward conditions of life will not disturb his inward peace nor the collapse of nations will not disturb the equilibrium of his mind
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that resignation to God’s will is the soul of happiness and keeps inward peace when outward conditions change; a foundational statement.

selected.text: causes of thy joy have ever been, and still are, beyond all mention and expression, sanctified above reckoning and the tongue’s recital. The first of these is turning unto the Most Exalted Horizon; the second, the recognition of the Lord of the kingdom of names; the third, the hearkening unto the call from the mouths of His chosen ones; the fourth, the beholding of His signs in the days of God. In brief, the causes of gladness are many. It is Our hope that henceforth thou mayest be happy of heart, joyous of soul, and gladdened in spirit, for
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lists the causes of the recipient’s joy, beginning with turning to the Most Exalted Horizon, and hopes he will be happy; gratitude enumerated.

selected.text: And thou, fear no one and grieve not for anything, but put thy trust in God. Verily He will protect thee from the hosts of Satan and will aid thee by His command and will provide thee with everlasting bounties and will give thee glad tidings of lights of ancient glory, that thou mayest abide in the Concourse on High and soar with two wings of longing unto the precincts of a mighty nearness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids fearing no one and trusting God, Who will protect and give everlasting bounties so the soul may soar with two wings of longing; courage and hope.

selected.text: Grieve not at anything. Put thy trust in God at all times. Verily, He will help thee as He helped thee before when thou wast heedless of the Cause. Then did We unveil the Beauty and manifest unto thee that which is better in thy Lord's sight than all that hath been created in the heavens and earth. We took thy hand with the hand of grace and power and delivered thee through Our sovereign might.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids trust at all times, recalling how God helped the recipient before and delivered him; trust grounded in remembered help.

selected.text: All this is from God's confirmations to His loved ones. Should He so desire, He would assist whomsoever hath turned unto Him to reform the entire world, and would seize, through His all-pervading sovereignty, from whomsoever He willeth, all that hath been and shall be. It behooveth the servant to commit all affairs unto Him and place his trust in Him. These are two mighty portals leading to the bounty and mercy of God, glorified be His majesty. We hope they
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh names committing all affairs to God and trusting Him as two mighty portals to His bounty and mercy; a memorable image.

selected.text: O true friends in Tehran, take note! In these days certain events have transpired in this prison, all of which are from the hidden ordinances and undoubted decrees. Therefore, we exiles, with utmost patience and tranquility and trust in the All-Merciful Lord, have bowed our heads in submission and have absolutely no grief, sorrow, anxiety or distress. We are confident in divine grace and bounties, and are gladdened by the holy spiritual breaths.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells the friends in Tehran that the exiles in prison, with patience and trust, have no grief or anxiety; steadfastness under imprisonment.

selected.text: I implore Thee, O Thou that turnest darkness into light, and revealest Thy mysteries on the Sinai of Thy Revelation, to aid me, at all times, to put my trust in Thee, and to commit mine affairs unto Thy care. Make me, then, O my God, content with that which the finger of Thy decree hath traced, and the pen of Thy ordinance hath written. Potent art Thou to do what pleaseth Thee, and in Thy grasp are the reins of all that are in heaven  and on earth

selected.text: Be as a zealous lion for God until He decrees with justice and thereafter brings about His Cause. Fear not the onslaught of the satans, for they are but uprooted shadows without proof, neither in the Book of Truth nor before creation, nor even in their own eyes. Their likeness is as the likeness of a dog: if thou attack it, it pants with its tongue out, and if thou leave it, it pants with its tongue out. Still their excessive panting with a mighty gift that thou mayest find rest from their evil. Draw not nigh unto those who have wronged lest their torment touch thee, for they have no life in them. Walk with them toward thy goal, for this
selected.reason: The Báb bids being as a zealous lion for God and not fearing the satans, yet keeping away from wrongdoers; courage with caution in its historical setting.

selected.text: God, exalted be His glory, hath said: "Verily, with hardship goeth ease." It is hoped that affairs will be set right. With the generous, tasks are not difficult. That soul should not be sorrowful. The affairs of the world have ever alternated between hardship and ease, yet bounty is from God and generosity from Him. Assuredly these hardships will be followed by mercy, and this difficulty by ease. Soon will He fulfill His promise and manifest that which beseemeth His might, His majesty and His generosity.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh cites the Qur’anic promise that with hardship goes ease and says the world’s affairs alternate between hardship and ease; a substantive consolation in difficulty.

selected.text: Unto God belongeth all authority from the beginning unto the end, and we all put our trust in God, our Lord, the All-Merciful. Sufficient unto us is God Who created us and all things by His command. He is the Mighty, the Well-Beloved. Say: He is the Ever-Living Who dieth not. Say: He is the One Who standeth over every soul, knowing what it hath earned and witnessing what it earneth. There is no God but He, the Mighty, the Well-Beloved. Say: God is my Lord, in Him have I placed my trust, and in God let the trusting place their trust. Say: God will suffice you against all things, while nothing sufficeth against God, Lord of the heavens and of the earth and of whatsoever lieth between them, Lord of all the worlds
selected.reason: The Báb’s fuller passage declaring all authority God’s, that God suffices against all things and that the trusting should place their trust in Him; the most complete statement from this source.
